source.title: Learning to Refuse: Towards Mitigating Privacy Risks in LLMs
source.authors: Zhenhua Liu; Tong Zhu; Chuan-Yuan Tan; Wen-Liang Chen

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates different unlearning methods on targeted personal-information QA and reports retained-set and downstream-task performance. It does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports unlearning scores and retained performance, not post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery, direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-based recovery. It also does not report whether attacks recover knowledge to the level of a model that never learned it.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a refusal-based unlearning method (NAUF) and a benchmark (RETURN). It reports only its own method and baselines on forget, retain and downstream scores for direct questions. It runs no relearning, ablation, quantization, rephrasing, jailbreak or other recovery attack, so it cannot bear on whether unlearning is shallow (B–E) or robust (A, F). Scoring well on direct forget-set questions is the method's own performance, not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude NAUF (with KLD regularization) beats the best baseline (RGD+GD) by 5.65 average unlearning points while keeping general ability. They evaluate no recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes name-aware refusal training with contrastive data augmentation and evaluates GA, NPO, RGD, and RDPO baselines; it does not reproduce the recovery-attack procedures named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with retain-set regularization (none, GD, KLD) and with inclusion of Contrastive Data Augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-relabelling unlearning trades forget-set suppression against retain-set accuracy. Without retain regularization, NAUF and RGD reach forget 100/96 but retain 0.06/3.16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-based unlearning of real individuals over-generalizes refusals to non-target individuals unless retain regularization is used.

record.problems: Experiments use LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and a limited set of deeply memorized individuals; the paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Forget Score is a relative decrease and does not itself show chance-level accuracy. No recovery attack or never-trained comparison is conducted.
record.rows_left_out: None from Table 2; all methods' Forget Score, Retain Score, and average downstream task accuracy results are included. Other downstream task-specific scores are not listed separately because the claim's general-capability check is represented by the reported average.

untested.parts: Robustness to any attack; near-chance accuracy, since Forget Score is a relative drop judged by an NLI model.
No direction ablation and no deletion-versus-blocking analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probing.
NAUF is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

record.verdict_notes: NAUF trains the model to refuse named individuals, i.e. access-blocking by design, but the paper never probes whether the knowledge remains. It is relevant context for C/F only as a candidate method that later attack studies could target. No uncertainty is reported, and there is a single model (LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct).

versions.untested_parts: Tests reduction in targeted-set performance and retention/general-task performance, but not whether simple attacks recover the information or whether performance reaches near-chance accuracy.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
No robustness evaluation against the listed recovery attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Unregularized methods and methods with retain-set regularization in Table 2
reader_labels.reason: The reported results show a trade-off: high Forget Scores can coincide with poor retain performance, while regularization improves retention; the scores do not establish chance-level post-unlearning accuracy or test recovery attacks (rows r07-r18, r25-r36, r43-r54).
